citations.quote: In general, we use an F-distributed test statistic to compare two variances.
To test a hypothesis about a slope, we calculate the test statistic by subtracting the hypothesized population slope
If the calculated t-statistic is outside the bounds of the critical t-values, we reject the null hypothesis

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: CFA L1 Reading 7 introduces the F-distributed test for the joint significance of regression slopes and the t-test on an individual slope coefficient (with `n − k − 1` df). At the L1 level, partial (nested) F-tests on multi-coefficient restrictions are not developed; the legacy card overreaches to multiple-regression machinery that is L2 / raw-econometric content.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Hypothesis Tests on a Fitted Regression
